knowledge:
- key_parameters: exp=An ExpressionSet or expression matrix containing log-transformed gene expression values ;; classes=A numeric vector of class labels (e.g., 1 and 2) indicating the experimental conditions, named with sample identifiers ;; graph=A graphNEL object representing the pathway topology ;; nperm=Number of permutations for the pathQ test ;; alphaV=Significance level for the variance test ;; b=Number of bootstrap replicates or iterations ;; method=Method used in easyClip (e.g., "mean" or "var") ;; trZero=Threshold below which values are treated as zero in clipper ;; permute=Logical indicating whether to permute in clipper ;; thr=Dissimilarity threshold for pruning overlapping paths in prunePaths
- alternatives: GSEA=Non-topological method that treats pathways as simple gene lists without structure ;; SPIA=Topological method that takes only a list of differentially expressed genes as input and tests a different null hypothesis ;; DEGraph=Another topological pathway analysis method on Bioconductor
- when_to_use: Use when you want to exploit pathway topology to identify both global pathway alterations (changes in mean expression and/or covariance/interaction strength) and specific sub-paths (portions of the pathway) driving the phenotypic differences between two conditions.
- pitfalls: The method is based on Gaussian graphical models, so it is strongly recommended to use log-transformed data ;; Ensure gene identifiers in the expression matrix/ExpressionSet match the node identifiers in the pathway graph (e.g., prefixing with "ENTREZID:" if using graphite) ;; RCytoscape is no longer supported on some platforms; RCy3 should be used instead for Cytoscape visualization

workflows.name: global_and_subpath_clipper_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform a two-step topological pathway analysis to test global pathway significance and identify specific active sub-paths.
input: expression_data.RData (ExpressionSet or matrix of log-transformed gene expression values)
class_labels.RData (numeric vector of class labels 1 and 2, named by sample)
workflows.stages: 1. Run global pathway analysis using pathQ to test for differences in covariance and mean ;; 2. Identify specific sub-paths associated with the phenotype using clipper ;; 3. Prune overlapping or redundant sub-paths using prunePaths ;; 4. Visualize the identified sub-paths using plotInCytoscape
workflows.code:
pathwayAnalysis <- pathQ(exp, classes, graph, nperm=100, alphaV=0.05, b=100)
pathwayAnalysis
clipped <- clipper(exp, classes, graph, "var", trZero=0.01, permute=FALSE)
clipped[,1:5]
clipped <- prunePaths(clipped, thr=0.2)
clipped[,1:5]
plotInCytoscape(graph, clipped[1,])

workflows.name: easy_clipper_analysis
workflows.intent: Quickly run a simplified topological pathway analysis to identify altered sub-paths and summarize results.
input: expression_data.RData (ExpressionSet or matrix of log-transformed gene expression values)
class_labels.RData (numeric vector of class labels 1 and 2, named by sample)
workflows.stages: 1. Run simplified analysis using easyClip with a specified method ;; 2. Summarize and inspect the results using easyLook
workflows.code:
clipped <- easyClip(exp, classes, graph, method="mean")
clipped[,1:5]
easyLook(clipped)
